Write a short blog post about what comes next for your digital team. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the post only.
final_message:
**What comes next for the team**

A year ago we set ourselves a simple goal: make it easier for people to do what they need to do with government, and cheaper for the taxpayer when they do. We have made real progress. Now it's time to be honest about what we've learned, and about what we need to change.

First, the good news. The services we have rebuilt around user needs are working better. Fewer people are phoning for help. Fewer forms are coming back with mistakes. Teams that once waited months for a change can now release something every fortnight. It's been a pleasure to watch, and I want to thank everyone who made it happen.

But let me be clear about the problem. Too much of this work has been done team by team, department by department. Each of us has solved the same problems in our own way: identity, payments, notifications, hosting. We have built good services on foundations that don't fit together. Siloed delivery doesn't scale, and we can't keep reinventing the wheel and expect different results.

So what comes next? Three things.

**Shared components, not shared slide decks.** We will concentrate on building a small number of common platforms that any team in government can pick up and use. Where something already exists and works, we will adopt it. Where it doesn't, we will build it once, in the open, and invite others to help.

**Data as the foundation.** None of this works if we can't trust and reuse the information government holds. We will put more effort into making data accurate, well governed and easy to find, so that services can be built on it rather than around it.

**Skills across the whole of government.** We need digital expertise in policy, legal, commercial and operational roles, not only in the delivery teams. So we will expand our work on training, mentoring and hiring, and we will be more open about the jobs that are available and the support on offer.

None of this is a fresh start. Much of the groundwork has been laid by colleagues across government, and my job is to join it up, not to replace it. I would like to hear from the people who have already done the hard thinking.

I should also say what we will stop doing. We will stop starting projects without asking whether someone else has already solved the problem. We will stop treating long contracts as the only way to buy technology. And we will stop measuring ourselves by how much we launch, and start measuring by whether people can get things done.

That's the plan, in short. It won't be quick, and it won't always be comfortable. But I'm confident that we have the people and the will to do it.

If you work in this area, or simply have a view, get in touch. I'm counting on your help.
